items.question: What is Astro?
items.answer: Astro is a modern web framework built for content-driven sites. It ships zero JavaScript by default — only sending what the page actually needs. The result is fast load times, excellent Core Web Vitals scores, and lean, maintainable code.

items.question: Why build with Astro?
items.answer: Astro is the right tool for content-heavy sites: minimal JavaScript, clean HTML, great SEO out of the box, and a developer experience that stays out of your way. It's lean, purposeful, and built to last.

items.question: What can I build with Astro Rocket?
items.answer: Portfolios, business sites, marketing pages, blogs, documentation sites — any content-driven project. Astro Rocket gives you the structure, components, and defaults to hit the ground running.

items.question: Is Astro Rocket listed on the official Astro themes directory?
items.answer: Yes. Astro Rocket is listed on the official Astro themes directory as a free, production-ready theme.

items.question: Will Astro Rocket keep up with new Astro releases?
items.answer: Yes. Astro Rocket is actively maintained and updated to track new Astro releases. Follow along on the blog or watch the GitHub repository for updates.

items.question: Is it free to use?
items.answer: Yes, completely free. Astro Rocket is MIT licensed — use it for personal and commercial projects, no attribution required.

items.question: How do I switch themes?
items.answer: Change a single line in your config. Astro Rocket ships with 8 hand-crafted colour themes — swap between them instantly without touching a line of CSS.

items.question: Does it support TypeScript?
items.answer: Yes, TypeScript is used throughout. All components, configs, and utilities are fully typed.

items.question: How do I add my own language for i18n?
items.answer: Astro Rocket's i18n is config-driven. Add your locale to the i18n config file, create a matching translation file, and the routing and UI adapt automatically.

items.question: Where do I report bugs or suggest features?
items.answer: Open an issue or start a discussion on the GitHub repository. Contributions and feedback are always welcome.

sandboxSeed.heading: Create your digital world
sandboxSeed.lead: Real cryptography, right in the browser: 12 words that exist nowhere else.
sandboxSeed.disclaimer: ⚠️ Demo: this phrase is real cryptography, but it is connected to nothing. It lives only on this page and vanishes when you leave. Do not use it as a real wallet.
sandboxSeed.copied: Copied to the clipboard. This is a convenience for testing. In real life you must write the seed down on paper. Press Hide — and the seed will be erased from this computer's memory, beyond recovery.
sandboxSeed.panelHidden: The seed is generated. This is the single most important secret of your world. Press Reveal to see it.
sandboxSeed.panelRevealed: The phrase is 128 bits of entropy packed into memorable words. The entire key hierarchy derives deterministically from it: Identity → Handle → SubHandle — the same seed yields the same keys on every device. Brute-forcing it is impossible: even a trillion guesses per second means billions of years.
sandboxSeed.paperPasteHint: Paste the seed from the clipboard here.
sandboxSeed.paperNote: Seed must be stored offline: paper — yes; screenshots, cloud notes, password managers — no. Electronic copies are attack surface. If these words leak, your identity leaks with them.
sandboxSeed.verifyPrompt: Enter words {a}, {b} and {c} of your seed phrase
sandboxSeed.verifyError: The words do not match your seed phrase. Check your notes.
sandboxSeed.verifySeeAgain: I need to see the seed phrase again
sandboxSeed.paperMissing: You haven't written the seed down. Go back and copy the seed onto your paper — a seed that isn't recorded cannot be kept.
sandboxSeed.paperBadgeHint: Click a word from your paper to fill the field.
sandboxSeed.bornText: The entire key hierarchy derives deterministically from these 12 words: Identity → Handle → SubHandle. Zero bytes on the server.
sandboxSeed.createdSequence: What just happened: you generated 128 bits of entropy in your browser — it derived your root Identity — you proved you hold the paper — your world exists. Nowhere along the way was a single byte stored on a server.

design.heading: Core entities
paragraphs: The core of the protocol: a root Identity derived from a seed phrase, contextual Handles, and stateless signed sessions.

Nothing here is stored or looked up: a server verifies a session with one signature check, and a third party verifies delegated access using only your root public key. Attestation chains carry audiences, scopes and TTL caps enforced at verification time — trust can be delegated, and revoked, without sharing a private key.

included.text: from 32 bytes or a 12/24-word phrase — constant forever, stored nowhere.
a separate Ed25519 keypair per context; compromising one reveals nothing about the others.
parent-signed grants with audiences, scopes and TTL caps, verified offline by any third party.
verifyStateless for your backend, verifyAttested for partners — with instant branch revocation.
deterministic passwords, channel keys and X25519 shared secrets, plus BIP39 passphrase support.

development.heading: End-to-end encryption
paragraphs: Protocol cryptography for real communication: canonical Signal X3DH, long-lived encrypted channels, and envelopes for recipients who are offline.

Channels derive a fresh key for every message and rotate epochs, so what was encrypted stays sealed even if a key leaks later. Pre-keys make asynchronous delivery work: you can encrypt for someone who hasn't been online for days. Underneath sit audited primitives — HKDF, X25519, AES-256-GCM — with Argon2id protecting passwords at the edges.

included.text: Signal's key agreement with mandatory one-time pre-keys — no zero-fallback, MITM-resistant.
per-message keys, strictly-increasing replay protection, epoch rotation at defined points.
X3DH-wrapped keys reach recipients who haven't been online; every envelope is self-contained.
named profiles for interactive and sensitive use, strength checks and HIBP breach lookup.
HKDF against RFC 5869 test vectors, X25519, AES-256-GCM, secure key wipe.

performance.heading: React SDK
paragraphs: React bindings that turn the protocol into product UI: identity hooks, seed-phrase screens, self-renewing sessions.

The seed phrase is the one secret users must never lose — so its UX is part of the security model. Words are shown once, verified by an order grid, validated word by word on import. Derived keys persist only as non-extractable CryptoKeys, isolated per identity. A headless layer keeps every state machine framework-agnostic — the future @me2em/sdk.

included.text: useCreateIdentity, useImportSeed, useHandle, useSubHandle — the full identity lifecycle.
show-once display, single copy, order-verification grid, per-word import validation.
useSession tracks expiry and auto-renews at half-life.
per-identity IndexedDB isolation with non-extractable persisted CryptoKeys.
framework-agnostic state machines with zero React imports.

process.heading: From seed to verified session
process.lead: Four steps — the same in every scenario, from a messenger to a charging network.

steps.title: Write the seed
steps.description: 12 or 24 BIP39 words on paper. The only permanent carrier of identity — never transmitted, never stored.

steps.title: Derive the root
steps.description: The Identity is computed locally by HKDF. Handles for each context — work, personal, devices — derive offline from it.

steps.title: Delegate & sign
steps.description: Attestation chains grant scoped, time-boxed access to devices, partners, and AI agents. Sessions are stateless signed tokens.

steps.title: Verify & revoke

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: The questions that come up before the first derivation.

items.question: Do I need to register anywhere?
items.answer: No. An Identity is derived from your seed phrase on your device. There is no account to create — and no database that could leak it.

items.question: What happens if I lose my seed phrase?
items.answer: The identity is unrecoverable — by design. The seed is the only permanent carrier of identity; there is no reset link because there is nothing on a server to reset.

items.question: Is Me2em a blockchain?
items.answer: No. Derivation and verification are pure cryptography — Ed25519 and HKDF — offline, with no network and no consensus. A session verifies in about a millisecond.

items.question: Is it production-ready?
items.answer: The packages are alpha (core 0.7, crypto 0.1, react 0.1), moving toward a v1.0 API freeze. Fine for evaluation and prototypes today; pin versions and expect changes in production.

items.question: Which verification mode should I use?
items.answer: verifyStateless for backends you control — they already hold the root key. verifyAttested for anyone else: grants are enforced at verification time, with the root public key only.

items.question: How deep can the hierarchy go?
items.answer: Identity → Handle → SubHandle, where SubHandle is the leaf (MAX_DEPTH = 2). A device derives its own SubHandles and child attestations — fully offline.

items.question: Can I revoke a device or an AI agent?
items.answer: Yes. Revoking one attestation jti disables the entire branch — current and future sessions — on every verifier that checks revocations.

items.question: Where do I report a vulnerability?
items.answer: See SECURITY.md in the me2em-protocol repository — responsible disclosure, with credit.

intro.heading: What Me2em is
intro.body: Me2em is a decentralized identity and authorization protocol built on Ed25519 cryptography and standard key-agreement primitives. Nothing to register, no passwords to store: a person, a device, or an AI agent is represented by keys derived locally from a single seed phrase. Every context keeps its own isolated identity, access is delegated and revoked through signed attestations, and servers confirm a session with a single signature check — serverless authentication with minimal latency that minimizes, or removes entirely, the database you have to run and protect. Me2em is for one user who safely becomes many: separate profiles (work, home, the gym), hierarchies of IoT devices and drones, autonomous AI agents under signed mandates, E2EE-encrypted channels, and deterministic passwords for third-party services.

workWithMe.heading: Guaranteed by cryptography
workWithMe.lead: Eight properties of the protocol — math, not promises.

cards.title: Seed-derived
cards.description: Your identity lives in a seed phrase; keys are recomputed on demand. A breached server holds nothing.

cards.title: Zero-knowledge
cards.description: Private keys never leave your device. Servers verify signatures without ever learning who you are.

cards.title: Deterministic
cards.description: Same seed, same keys — always. One identity on every device, with nothing to sync.

cards.title: Isolated
cards.description: Every Handle is a separate keypair. Compromising one context reveals nothing about the others.

cards.title: Stateless
cards.description: No session database. Any server — or any third party — verifies a token with one signature check.

cards.title: Delegatable
cards.description: Attestation chains hand scoped, time-boxed access to partners, IoT devices, and AI agents.

cards.title: Hierarchical
cards.description: Identity → Handle → SubHandle: a whole device fleet under one root, provisioned offline.

cards.title: Revocable
cards.description: One revoked attestation disables an entire branch — current and future sessions, instantly.
